places.name: Taj Mahal
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the Seven Wonders of the World, built 1632–1653 by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. The white Makrana marble mausoleum changes colour through the day — rosy at dawn, white at noon, golden at dusk. Closed on Fridays. Entry fees vary by nationality; foreigners significantly higher. Book tickets online to avoid queues.
places.openingDays: Sat–Thu 06:00–18:30 (closed Fri; open full moon nights)

places.name: Agra Fort
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — massive red sandstone fort begun by Emperor Akbar in 1565, later expanded by Jahangir and Shah Jahan. Houses a palace complex including the Diwan-i-Khas, Diwan-i-Aam, Moti Masjid and the octagonal tower from which Shah Jahan supposedly viewed the Taj Mahal in his final years. 2.5km walk inside. Budget 2 hours.

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — former Mughal capital built by Akbar in 1571, abandoned after 14 years reportedly due to water scarcity. The well-preserved ghost city includes the Buland Darwaza (170ft victory gate), Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal and Diwan-i-Khas. 40km from Agra; a half-day excursion. The site is separate from the adjacent dargah of Salim Chishti (free entry).

places.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah
places.description: First Mughal structure built entirely in marble (1628), mausoleum of Mirza Ghiyas Beg, Empress Nur Jahan's father. Often called the 'Baby Taj' for its marble lattice screens and pietra dura inlay that prefigure the Taj Mahal. Smaller and less crowded than the main monuments; set in a formal garden on the east bank of the Yamuna. Budget 1 hour.

places.name: Mehtab Bagh
places.description: Moonlight Garden directly opposite the Taj Mahal on the north bank of the Yamuna. Built by Babur in 1530 as the last of eleven gardens, it offers the best unobstructed sunset view of the Taj reflected in the river. Far less crowded than the Taj itself; entry by ASI ticket. Best visited late afternoon.

places.name: Sikandra — Akbar's Tomb
places.description: Mausoleum of Emperor Akbar, begun by Akbar himself and completed by his son Jahangir in 1613, 10km north-west of Agra. Blends Hindu, Islamic, Buddhist and Jain architectural motifs. Set in a 119-acre garden with roaming deer. Usually quiet even during peak season; a worthy alternative to the main monuments. Budget 1 hour.

places.name: Jama Masjid Agra
places.description: Grand mosque built in 1648 by Jahanara Begum, Shah Jahan's daughter, directly opposite Agra Fort. Dedicated to her spiritual guide Mian Mir, a Sufi saint. Free entry; visitors must remove shoes and dress modestly. Less visited than the main monuments but architecturally significant with its ribbed domes and sandstone courtyard.

places.name: Chini Ka Rauza
places.description: Tomb of Allama Afzel Khan Mullah Shukrullah of Shiraz, a Persian poet-scholar who served in Shah Jahan's court. Completed 1635; notable for Persian-glazed tile (chini = Chinese/ceramic) work on the exterior dome and walls — unusual for Mughal architecture. Rarely visited; a peaceful and atmospheric hidden gem north of the main monument circuit.

places.name: Aram Bagh
places.description: Ram Bagh — the oldest Mughal garden in India, laid out by Babur in 1528 as a rest garden with terraced lawns descending to the Yamuna. The geometric chaharbagh design became the template for later Mughal gardens including Humayun's tomb and the Taj. Rarely visited; entry ticket from ASI.

places.name: Kinari Bazaar
places.description: Agra's old city market, primarily known for zari (embroidery), shoes, marble inlay items (pietra dura) and petha (Agra's famous sweet made from ash gourd). The lanes are narrow and best explored on foot. The marble inlay craft heritage draws from the same artisan lineage that worked on the Taj Mahal; workshops are open for viewing.
